en: Mayon Volcano erupts liquid magma that cools into solid igneous rock.
The Filipino dessert halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture of shaved ice, sweet beans, and fruits.
Making taho involves a chemical change where soy milk coagulates into solid silken tofu.
Asin tibok from Bohol is a solid mixture of sea salt and coconut husk ash.
The Banaue Rice Terraces use the physical property of clay soil to hold liquid water.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River contains water vapor that condenses into liquid droplets on cave walls.
The Philippine Eagle's hollow feathers trap gas air to provide thermal insulation.
Rusting of the iron roof of the Malolos Cathedral is a chemical change forming iron oxide.
The engine block of a traditional Filipino jeepney is cast from a solid mixture of iron and carbon.
The waling-waling orchid absorbs liquid water through its roots to maintain turgor pressure in its solid leaves.
White sand on Boracay beach is a solid mixture of crushed coral and quartz minerals.
Weaving piña fibers from the pineapple plant into a Barong Tagalog is a physical change.
